title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
summary: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today s epic patch batch dwarfs September s record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.
card_summary: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today s epic patch batch dwarfs September s record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal…

sections.overview: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today s epic patch batch dwarfs September s record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.
sections.technical:
At least 78 of the flaws fixed this month are rated critical, meaning they could be exploited with little or no action by the user, and most of those critical bugs allow an attacker to execute code of their choice on the vulnerable system. While Microsoft said there are no signs anyone is exploiting it yet, a security feature bypass in the .NET Framework ( CVE-2026-108398 ) was publicly disclosed prior to today, potentially giving attackers advance time to work out how to exploit the bug. Microsoft credits large language models for the high volume of bug discovery, and presumably AI gets credit for many of the patches used to fix these flaw. Just one of the weaknesses patched this week is considered a zero day, or already exploited in the wild.

Referenced vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-108398, CVE-2026-96951.
sections.impact:
CVE-2026-96951 is a security feature bypass in the Windows Shell that affects Windows 10 and 11 systems, as well as some Server versions. Windows 10 users might be wondering if they can still expect security updates after this month. At least 78 of the flaws fixed this month are rated critical, meaning they could be exploited with little or no action by the user, and most of those critical bugs allow an attacker to execute code of their choice on the vulnerable system.

Assessed severity: CRITICAL.
sections.context: This story is part of the recurring zero-day pattern where exploitation pressure is highest before broad patch adoption.

email_summary: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Tracked as CVE-2026-108398, CVE-2026-96951. Severity is rated critical.

summary: An attacker chained three zero-day flaws in Ivanti Connect Secure, a VPN appliance, to run commands as root without logging in, security firm Volexity said on October 13.
